day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Vancouver International Airport at 12:00 PM on Flight AC. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the Canada Line SkyTrain directly from YVR Airport Station to downtown Vancouver — a budget-friendly ~$4 CAD ride taking about 25 minutes. Check in to Vancouver Harbour Stay and get oriented in the neighbourhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Granville Island Public Market Food Tour. Explore the vibrant indoor market, sample local artisan cheeses, fresh Pacific salmon, baked goods, and seasonal produce from vendor stalls. This is a great low-cost way to graze and eat lunch while soaking up Vancouver's iconic food culture. Take the False Creek mini-ferry from downtown for ~$4 CAD each way.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the False Creek seawall back toward downtown as the sun begins to lower. Enjoy the harbour views and mountain backdrop. Wind down with a relaxed evening near the hotel to recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and snack at the airport or on the SkyTrain — budget ~$5–8 CAD
meals.lunch: Graze through Granville Island Public Market stalls — try a fresh salmon slider, artisan bread, and local cheese for ~$15–20 CAD total
meals.dinner: Davie Street or Robson Street area near downtown: try Phnom Penh Restaurant for legendary butter beef and garlic squid (~$18–22 CAD per person) or grab a filling banh mi from a local Vietnamese deli for ~$7–9 CAD

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light given the noon arrival. The Canada Line SkyTrain is the most budget-friendly airport transfer (~$4 CAD vs ~$40+ CAD taxi). Granville Island is walkable or accessible via a cheap mini-ferry. Keep energy for bigger days ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Early start for the Lynn Canyon Suspension Bridge & Ecology Centre Hike. Take TransLink buses from downtown to North Vancouver (about 45–60 min, ~$3.25 CAD with a Compass Card). Hike through old-growth temperate rainforest, cross the FREE suspension bridge (unlike Capilano, this one costs nothing!), and visit the Ecology Centre to learn about the local ecosystem. Trails are well-marked and suitable for most fitness levels.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Lynn Canyon's network of trails — the Baden Powell Trail section and the Twin Falls loop are scenic and free. Pack a picnic lunch to enjoy creekside. Head back to downtown by mid-afternoon via TransLink.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Sunset Dinner at Steveston Village Wharf experience. Take the Canada Line to Brighouse Station in Richmond, then a short bus ride to historic Steveston Village (~$3.25 CAD). Buy ultra-fresh Dungeness crab, spot prawns, or wild salmon directly from the fishing boats docked at the wharf — some of the freshest and most affordable seafood in the region. Eat at the dockside picnic tables as the sun sets over the Fraser River.

meals.breakfast: Grab oatmeal, a banana, and coffee from a grocery store or Tim Hortons near the hotel — budget ~$5–7 CAD. Pack snacks for the hike.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic to eat in Lynn Canyon Park — pick up items the night before from a local grocery store (bread, deli meat, fruit, water) for ~$8–10 CAD
meals.dinner: Steveston Wharf fresh catch — a whole Dungeness crab or a bag of spot prawns direct from fishing boats runs ~$20–30 CAD and feeds 1–2 people generously. BYOB seasoning or grab condiments from a nearby convenience store.

day_by_day.notes: Lynn Canyon is one of Vancouver's best-kept budget secrets — the suspension bridge and all trails are completely FREE. Bring sturdy walking shoes and layers as the forest is cool even in June. For Steveston, check boat availability in advance as catch times vary; the wharf is most active in the afternoon. Load a Compass Card for seamless transit all day.

day_by_day.morning: Stanley Park Seawall Cycle & Nature Exploration. Rent a bike from one of the rental shops near the park entrance on Denman Street (~$8–12 CAD/hour or ~$30–40 CAD for a half-day). Ride the iconic 10 km seawall loop at your own pace, enjoying panoramic views of the mountains, Burrard Inlet, Lions Gate Bridge, and English Bay. Stop at Siwash Rock, Third Beach, and the totem poles in the park interior.
day_by_day.afternoon: Lock up your bike and explore Stanley Park on foot — visit the free rose garden, Beaver Lake trail, and enjoy the lush old-growth forest. Head to English Bay Beach in the late afternoon to relax on the sand, people-watch, and take in the views of the North Shore mountains. English Bay is one of Vancouver's most beloved free spots.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along Denman Street and Davie Street in the West End neighbourhood — a lively, affordable dining strip. Browse the restaurants and pick a budget-friendly dinner spot. End the evening with a scoop of ice cream from a local shop and a sunset walk along the beach.

meals.breakfast: Grab a fresh bagel with cream cheese and coffee from a local café on Denman Street near the park — budget ~$8–10 CAD
meals.lunch: Pick up a fresh wrap or sandwich from a grocery store deli (Whole Foods on Robson or a local IGA) and eat on a Stanley Park bench or at Second Beach — ~$10–12 CAD
meals.dinner: Denman Street West End dining: try The Naam (Vancouver's legendary vegetarian restaurant, open 24 hrs, mains ~$14–18 CAD) or grab wood-fired pizza by the slice from a local spot for ~$8–10 CAD

day_by_day.notes: Bike rentals are cheapest when booked for a half-day block rather than hourly. The seawall is flat and suitable for all cycling levels. June days are long in Vancouver (sunset ~9:15 PM), so there is plenty of daylight to enjoy the park and beach well into the evening. Bring sunscreen and a light rain layer just in case.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Commercial Drive neighbourhood ('The Drive') — Vancouver's bohemian, multicultural hub. Browse independent coffee roasters (try Prado Café or JJ Bean for a ~$4–5 CAD flat white), peek into local bookshops, vintage stores, and murals. This is a great neighbourhood to experience authentic, non-touristy Vancouver on a budget.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Dr. Sun Yat-Sen Classical Chinese Garden in Chinatown (admission ~$14 CAD, or view the free adjacent public park). Wander through historic Chinatown, one of North America's oldest, and explore Strathcona neighbourhood's colourful street art and community gardens. Head back to the hotel to pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in Vancouver — return to Granville Island or try Main Street's affordable dining strip. Celebrate the trip with a local craft beer from a neighbourhood brewery taproom (many offer pints for ~$7–9 CAD) paired with a budget-friendly meal. Head to the airport via Canada Line SkyTrain if departing tonight, or enjoy a relaxed final evening near the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Linger over a proper breakfast at a Commercial Drive café — try a breakfast burrito or avocado toast with coffee for ~$12–15 CAD
meals.lunch: Chinatown has incredible budget eats — try a steaming bowl of wonton noodle soup or BBQ pork rice from a traditional Chinese diner for ~$10–13 CAD
meals.dinner: Main Street craft brewery taproom dinner: order shareable snacks or a burger at a local brewpub like 33 Acres Brewing or Brassneck Brewery — budget ~$20–25 CAD including a pint

day_by_day.notes: The Dr. Sun Yat-Sen Garden free public park adjacent to the paid garden still offers beautiful views at no cost if budget is tight. Commercial Drive is best explored on foot and is well-served by the 99 B-Line and No. 20 buses from downtown (~$3.25 CAD). Keep your Compass Card loaded for the airport SkyTrain on departure day to avoid paying the premium cash fare.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Vancouver International Airport at 12:00 PM on Flight AC. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the Canada Line SkyTrain directly from YVR to downtown Vancouver (approx. 25 min, ~$4 CAD). Check in to Vancouver Harbour Stay and freshen up. Take a leisurely orientation stroll along the Coal Harbour waterfront promenade to get your bearings and soak in the harbour views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Granville Island Public Market Food Tour — explore Vancouver's iconic market, sampling local artisan cheeses, fresh Pacific salmon, handmade charcuterie, baked goods, and seasonal produce. Spend 2–3 hours wandering the stalls, chatting with vendors, and soaking up the lively atmosphere. Browse the artisan shops and galleries surrounding the market.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into the neighbourhood with a relaxed dinner at a well-regarded local restaurant near the hotel. Wind down with a walk along the Coal Harbour seawall as the sun sets over the North Shore mountains.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and pastry at the airport or on arrival — skip a formal breakfast given the midday landing.
meals.lunch: Graze through Granville Island Public Market stalls — build a meal from fresh oysters, artisan bread, local cheeses, and a BC craft cider (budget ~$20–30 CAD).
meals.dinner: Forage Kitchen or The Flying Pig Gastown — farm-to-table Pacific Northwest cuisine with seasonal ingredients. Expect ~$45–65 CAD per person including a drink.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light given the midday arrival and potential travel fatigue. Store large luggage at the hotel before the Granville Island visit. Granville Island is best reached by False Creek Ferry from downtown (a fun ~5-min ride, ~$5 CAD) or a short cab/rideshare. Confirm hotel check-in time in advance in case early check-in is needed.

day_by_day.morning: Early start for the Stanley Park Seawall Cycle & Nature Exploration. Rent bikes from Spokes Bicycle Rentals at the park entrance (open from 8 AM, ~$15–20 CAD/hr). Ride the iconic 10 km seawall loop, stopping at Siwash Rock, Third Beach, Prospect Point for sweeping views of Lions Gate Bridge and the North Shore mountains, and the totem poles at Brockton Point. Allow 2.5–3 hours at a relaxed pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: After cycling, return bikes and explore Stanley Park's interior trails on foot — visit Beaver Lake and the ancient forest paths. In the mid-afternoon, head back toward the West End and spend time in the Robson Street area for window shopping and a coffee break. Visit English Bay Beach to relax on the sand.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Gastown for dinner, Vancouver's historic cobblestone neighbourhood. Explore the steam clock and Victorian architecture before sitting down to eat.

meals.breakfast: Café Medina in downtown Vancouver — famous for Belgian waffles, lavender lattes, and Mediterranean-inspired brunch. Arrive early (opens 8 AM) to beat the queue. Budget ~$20–28 CAD.
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch from a nearby deli or grab fish tacos and a cold drink from a Stanley Park concession stand near Second Beach. Budget ~$15–20 CAD.
meals.dinner: Tacofino Gastown or Wildebeest Restaurant — Tacofino for casual, flavourful Pacific tacos (~$20–30 CAD); Wildebeest for a more elevated farm-to-table experience (~$55–75 CAD per person).

day_by_day.notes: June in Vancouver means long daylight hours (sunset around 9:15 PM), perfect for an evening walk after dinner. Bike rentals are popular — consider booking Spokes in advance or arriving right at opening. Wear layers as the seawall can be breezy even in June.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day adventure: Lynn Canyon Suspension Bridge & Ecology Centre Hike. Take a TransLink bus (Route 228 from Lynn Valley Road, ~45 min from downtown) or a rideshare to Lynn Canyon Park. Begin with a visit to the free Ecology Centre to learn about the temperate rainforest ecosystem. Cross the free suspension bridge — a thrilling alternative to the commercial Capilano bridge — and hike the Twin Falls Trail and 30-Foot Pool loop through towering old-growth Douglas firs and cedar trees.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Lynn Canyon's trail network — the Baden Powell Trail section offers more immersive old-growth forest scenery. Swim or wade (carefully) at the 30-Foot Pool if weather permits. Pack a trail lunch and rest by the canyon creek. Head back to North Vancouver by mid-afternoon and explore the Lonsdale Quay Market for local snacks and artisan goods before taking the scenic SeaBus ferry back to downtown Waterfront Station (12-min crossing, ~$3.25 CAD).
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening near the hotel. Stroll along the Coal Harbour waterfront as float planes land and sailboats return to harbour. Enjoy a casual dinner in the Yaletown neighbourhood.

meals.breakfast: Jam Café on Beatty Street — creative, hearty brunch classics with local ingredients. Arrive early to avoid a wait. Budget ~$18–25 CAD.
meals.lunch: Pack a trail lunch from a downtown deli or grab supplies from a Granville Street grocery store the night before — sandwiches, fruit, trail mix, and water. Budget ~$12–18 CAD.
meals.dinner: Yaletown Brewing Company — a beloved local brewpub with wood-fired pizza, hearty mains, and excellent BC craft beers in a converted heritage warehouse. Budget ~$35–50 CAD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Wear sturdy walking shoes or light hiking boots for Lynn Canyon. Bring a rain layer — the rainforest canopy can drip even on clear days. The park is free to enter, making this an excellent mid-range budget day. The SeaBus return offers stunning views of the Vancouver skyline — try to time it for golden hour.

day_by_day.morning: For the grand finale, embark on the Garibaldi Provincial Park Panorama Ridge Day Hike — a breathtaking full-day experience. Depart from Vancouver by 6:30–7:00 AM via rideshare or rental car to the Rubble Creek trailhead near Squamish (approx. 1.5 hrs). The hike to Panorama Ridge is ~30 km return with significant elevation gain, rewarding you with legendary views over turquoise Garibaldi Lake, the Black Tusk volcanic peak, and endless alpine wilderness. Start early to maximize daylight and avoid afternoon crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the hike at your own pace — the Panorama Ridge summit is the goal for the most dramatic panoramic views. Rest, eat lunch at the top, and take in one of the most iconic vistas in British Columbia. Begin the descent in the early afternoon to ensure a comfortable return before dark.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Vancouver by early evening, tired but exhilarated. Treat yourself to a well-earned celebratory dinner at a special restaurant to close out the trip — something that honours Vancouver's incredible local seafood and Pacific Northwest culinary identity.

meals.breakfast: Early, energy-rich breakfast at the hotel or a quick stop at a Tim Hortons or local café en route — oatmeal, eggs, and coffee. Budget ~$10–15 CAD. Pack extra snacks for the trail.
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch is essential — hearty sandwiches, energy bars, nuts, dried fruit, and at least 2L of water per person. Prepare the night before. Budget ~$15 CAD.
meals.dinner: Blue Water Café in Yaletown — Vancouver's premier seafood restaurant, celebrated for its raw bar, BC Dungeness crab, and wild salmon. A worthy splurge to end the trip (~$75–100 CAD per person). Alternatively, Ancora Waterfront Dining for a similar mid-to-upscale seafood experience with harbour views.

day_by_day.notes: Panorama Ridge is a strenuous, full-day hike — only attempt it if your group is physically fit and experienced with long-distance hiking. Check BC Parks trail conditions and weather forecast the night before at bcparks.ca. Bring trekking poles, sun protection, a rain layer, and bear spray (rentable in Squamish). If energy levels are lower after Day 3, consider substituting with the more accessible Sunset Dinner at Steveston Village Wharf experience instead — a relaxed, scenic half-day trip for ultra-fresh Dungeness crab and waterfront views.

Check-in, freshen up, and settle into your harbour-view suite. Take a leisurely stroll along the Coal Harbour waterfront promenade to orient yourself with the stunning surroundings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Granville Island Public Market Food Tour: Head to the iconic Granville Island Public Market (approximately 15 minutes from the hotel via private car or water taxi). Explore artisan cheese stalls, fresh Pacific salmon, handcrafted charcuterie, local bakeries, and BC wines. Engage with local vendors and sample the best of Vancouver's culinary scene in a relaxed, immersive setting.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset stroll through Yaletown, Vancouver's upscale neighbourhood just minutes from the hotel. Enjoy cocktails at a rooftop bar overlooking False Creek before a refined dinner at one of the city's premier waterfront restaurants.

meals.breakfast: N/A – mid-day arrival; grab a light snack or fresh juice at the hotel upon check-in
meals.lunch: Granville Island Public Market grazing experience – artisan cheeses, smoked Pacific salmon, fresh-baked sourdough, and local charcuterie paired with a glass of BC Okanagan white wine
meals.dinner: Ancora Waterfront Dining & Patio (Coal Harbour) – celebrated Peruvian-Japanese fusion with premium Pacific seafood, outstanding harbour views, and an award-winning sake and cocktail menu

day_by_day.notes: Request a harbour or mountain view room at check-in. Book the Granville Island food tour in advance. Consider a private water taxi from Granville Island back to Coal Harbour for a scenic end to the afternoon. Ancora reservations should be made well ahead of travel.

day_by_day.morning: Stanley Park Seawall Cycle & Nature Exploration: Begin the day with a premium bike rental (or private guided cycling experience) along the iconic 10 km Stanley Park Seawall. Enjoy panoramic views of the North Shore mountains, Burrard Inlet, and English Bay. Stop at Prospect Point Lookout for dramatic views of Lions Gate Bridge. Explore interior forest trails and visit the famous totem poles at Brockton Point.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue into the heart of Stanley Park on foot or by bike, visiting Beaver Lake and the ancient forest interior. After the park, head to Robson Street or the South Granville gallery district for premium boutique shopping and a relaxed afternoon coffee at a specialty café.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel to refresh before an elegant evening out in the Gastown historic district. Explore cobblestone streets, visit curated local art galleries, and enjoy a world-class tasting menu dinner.

meals.breakfast: In-room or hotel restaurant breakfast – smoked salmon eggs benedict, fresh BC fruit, and locally roasted single-origin coffee
meals.lunch: The Teahouse Restaurant in Stanley Park – a Vancouver institution set within the park itself, offering West Coast cuisine with garden and ocean views; try the Dungeness crab cake and grilled halibut
meals.dinner: Hawksworth Restaurant (Downtown Vancouver) – one of Vancouver's most celebrated fine dining establishments; seasonal tasting menu featuring locally sourced BC ingredients with impeccable wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Start the Seawall ride by 9:00 AM to enjoy cooler temperatures and fewer crowds. Bike rentals are available near the park entrance on Denman Street; premium e-bike or guided options are recommended. Hawksworth tasting menus require advance reservation and should be booked prior to travel.

day_by_day.morning: Garibaldi Provincial Park – Panorama Ridge Full-Day Hike: Depart early (by 7:00 AM) via private luxury vehicle transfer to Garibaldi Provincial Park, approximately 75 km north of Vancouver. Embark on the breathtaking Panorama Ridge trail – a challenging but extraordinarily rewarding full-day hike through old-growth forest, alpine meadows, and past the stunning turquoise Garibaldi Lake. Panorama Ridge summit offers one of the most spectacular wilderness panoramas in British Columbia.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the hike, descending through wildflower meadows and glacial terrain. The full Panorama Ridge route is approximately 30 km return and takes 8–10 hours. Enjoy a gourmet packed picnic lunch prepared by the hotel at a scenic alpine rest point near the lake.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Vancouver by private transfer (arriving approximately 6:30–7:00 PM). Relax with a soak in the hotel spa or bath, then enjoy a quieter but equally refined dinner close to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast box or in-room dining before 7:00 AM departure – smoked salmon bagel, fresh fruit, granola, and a thermos of premium coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet hotel-prepared trail picnic – artisan sandwiches with BC charcuterie, local cheeses, fresh fruit, energy bars, and sparkling water; enjoyed at Garibaldi Lake viewpoint
meals.dinner: Blue Water Café (Yaletown) – Vancouver's premier raw bar and seafood restaurant; indulge in a seafood tower with BC oysters, spot prawns, and Dungeness crab, paired with a curated BC or Burgundy wine selection

day_by_day.notes: This is a strenuous full-day hike – proper footwear, layered clothing, sun protection, and ample water are essential. Arrange the packed lunch with the hotel concierge the evening before. A private guided hiking option with a local naturalist guide is highly recommended for an enriched experience. Check trail conditions and park permits in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Lynn Canyon Suspension Bridge & Ecology Centre Hike: Head north across the Second Narrows Bridge to Lynn Canyon Park in North Vancouver (approximately 25 minutes from the hotel). Hike through old-growth temperate rainforest, cross the free suspension bridge over the dramatic canyon gorge, and visit the Ecology Centre to learn about the coastal forest ecosystem. Enjoy serene forest pools, waterfalls, and towering Douglas firs in a far less crowded setting than Capilano.
day_by_day.afternoon: Sunset Dinner at Steveston Village Wharf experience begins with an early afternoon departure to historic Steveston Village in Richmond (approximately 35 minutes from the hotel). Visit the working fishing wharf to purchase ultra-fresh Dungeness crab, spot prawns, and wild Pacific salmon directly from the boats. Explore the charming heritage village, the Gulf of Georgia Cannery National Historic Site, and the waterfront boardwalk.
day_by_day.evening: Cook your fresh Steveston catch in a curated private dining experience – arrange with the hotel for a private chef to prepare your market-fresh seafood in a suite or private dining room. Alternatively, enjoy a final celebratory dinner at one of Vancouver's iconic rooftop restaurants with sweeping city and mountain views before departure preparations.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel restaurant breakfast – full West Coast spread including house-smoked salmon, BC eggs, seasonal fruit, avocado toast on artisan bread, and fresh-pressed juice
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch at Lynn Canyon Park – premium charcuterie, local cheeses, fresh baguette, and sparkling water enjoyed beside the canyon creek
meals.dinner: Private in-suite chef experience at Vancouver Harbour Stay using Steveston-fresh Dungeness crab and spot prawns – steamed crab with drawn butter, garlic prawn linguine, and a chilled bottle of BC Okanagan Chardonnay; OR CinCin Ristorante rooftop terrace for a refined Italian-West Coast farewell dinner with panoramic views

day_by_day.notes: Lynn Canyon is free to enter and far less commercialised than Capilano – ideal for an authentic nature experience. Arrive at Steveston Wharf between 1:00–3:00 PM for the best selection of fresh catch directly off the boats. Coordinate the private chef dinner experience with the hotel concierge at least 48 hours in advance. Begin packing and confirm departure logistics this evening.
